verdicts.evidence: Checks I ran on dce59515 (built dist is newer than the last source commit). Held-out checks: freeze.test.ts 4/4 passed; proof.test.ts 20 passed, 4 skipped. Visible frozen checks in packages/cli/test/meaning-roles/freeze: 59/59 passed in 724s. I then probed fresh repositories wired the way the cli README says (.git/hooks/reference-transaction runs `exec cratylus freeze-gate "$@"`), plus one throwaway copy of this repository with its husky wiring. Setup in each: library cut 'renewal', architect=architect; frozen check checks/renewal.test.ts, which uses checks/support/access.ts and lib/patron.ts; the ledger committed as this repository commits it. The baselines held: the lead's commit of the example was refused naming cut, architect and path; the architect's commit and supersede were admitted; the lead's supersede was refused. The routes in the finding still reached the record.
verdicts.finding: Each case below is a lead (CRATYLUS_AGENT=lead) whose change ends up recorded. None of them sets a name by hand (0130) or switches the hooks off (0131). (1) The freeze is read from the working copy, not from the record: frozen.ts, uses.ts, cut.ts and ledger.ts all read the working tree. (a) `mv design/ledger <elsewhere>`, then commit the relaxed design/examples/library/renewal.md: admitted. `concepts retire renewal` is then appended and its commit admitted. After moving the ledger back, the branch holds both changes. (b) A hand-written {kind:'integrate',transition:'integrate:renewal',cut:'renewal'} file in the working copy's ledger, carrying no agent: the commit of the relaxed example is admitted, and the freeze is back once the file is removed. (c) `git --work-tree=<dir holding only the edited example> add … && commit`: admitted, with the project's working copy untouched. (d) An uncommitted edit renaming the examples' '(renewal)' tag: the lead's `concepts supersede renewal` is appended to the journal; with the edit still in place, `concepts retire renewal` is appended and committed too. This fails 24, 25, 31-33, 36 and 38. (e) An uncommitted edit dropping the check's import, or moving the check out of the working copy: the lead's commits of checks/support/access.ts (made to accept anyone) and of lib/patron.ts are admitted. 0128 says a working-copy change is not the frozen check, yet here it decides what is frozen. (2) `workPackage update work --output src/ --output checks/support/`, which anyone may run, empties `uses`. The lead's weakening commit of the fixture is then admitted: example 33, weaken its check. (3) The history judges a journal entry only by the kind the entry declares at the new tip. Three commits with --no-verify are admitted: an in-place rewrite of renewal's define entry (its history now shows only the rewritten wording); `git rm` of the architect's committed supersede entry (renewal is back to its earlier meaning); and a hand-written second define entry (renewal becomes competing, with no current meaning). This fails 24's 'current meaning and history stay unchanged'. (4) Pushes into the repository are not held. In a README-wired repository, the lead's `git push . <detached commit>:refs/heads/main` and a push from a clone to a new branch are admitted: the hook runs in $GIT_DIR, topOf() is undefined there, and freezeGate admits silently, though a freeze that cannot be read should refuse. In a copy of this repository, `git push --no-verify . <commit>:refs/heads/feature/meaning-roles` moved the cut's branch to a change of workflow/24. GIT_TRACE shows no reference-transaction hook ran: the relative core.hooksPath `.husky/_` resolves against $GIT_DIR. The same wiring runs no hook in a linked worktree (`git worktree add`): a commit there and `git update-ref refs/heads/feature/meaning-roles` both went through. (5) `git replace <tip> <variant with relaxed example>` touches no branch. The lead's next ordinary commit then carries the relaxed example into main, and it is admitted, because the gate's diff-tree follows the replacement.

verdicts.evidence: The journal's refusal itself is sound: unfrozen() runs before append for supersede and retire, and the baselines and probes S, held-out 1 and 2, and visible 24, 25, 34 and 38 hold. But the concepts it protects are read from the working copy's example tags, and the history accepts journal rewrites and deletions.
verdicts.finding: Three ways the lead still changes a frozen concept. An uncommitted edit of design/examples/library/renewal.md that changes '(renewal)' to '(loan)' gets the lead's `concepts supersede renewal --wording 'staff-only renewal'` appended (history: define, then the lead's supersede); with the edit kept, the lead's retire is appended and committed. A commit with --no-verify that rewrites renewal's define entry in place, or deletes the architect's supersede entry, is admitted by the history; both are rewrites, which supersession says never happen. A hand-written second `define` entry for renewal is admitted and leaves it competing. Each fails examples 24, 25, 33 and 38, and held-out 2 in spirit: the architect's correction stops being current when the lead deletes it.

verdicts.evidence: Each cut is scoped to its context and lasts until integrated. Probe S: the lead's supersede and retire of opening-hours were admitted, journal and commit (28). museum/renewal was admitted while library/renewal was refused (29). The lead's integrate was refused and the architect's admitted; afterwards the lead's supersede was appended as a new version with the define and retire kept, and the lead's example commit was admitted (30, 37). Held-out 1 (two cuts, one integrated) and visible 38 pass. `open` refuses contexts held by different architects, and integrate is architect-only (F4 passes). The forged-integrate and absent-ledger routes are a defect in how the freeze is read, reported under freeze.

The binding works. Every bash call is led by `export CRATYLUS_AGENT='<session agent>'`, or by `unset` in a session that is no agent. The attempt-time gate is retired. A builder's dispatch is refused while an example its package owns is unchecked. Visible 35's main and sub cases and F1/F6 pass. But this package owns workflow/31, 32, 33 and 36, and they do not hold end to end. Every failing route is in packages/runtime and the repository wiring, which are freeze-record's outputs. My probes found nothing in this package's own outputs to change.
verdicts.finding: Example 31 fails: once approved, the example can still be changed by commit: by moving the ledger out of the working copy, by a hand-written integrate entry, by `git --work-tree`, by `git push .` or a push from a clone, by a linked worktree (this repository's wiring), or after `git replace`. Example 33 fails: the check can be weakened through `workPackage update --output checks/support/`. The dispatch gate this package adds can also be met without a frozen check binding the example: an uncommitted edit adding 'library/3' to the frozen check file empties `unchecked`, though HEAD's check never names library/3. Route these back to freeze-record.

hardeningNotes: Meaning question for the architect, since it decides the fix and the frozen fixture: what is the freeze read from? The visible fixture keeps the ledger uncommitted ('where cratylus keeps it'), while this repository tracks design/ledger/ in its history. Reading the freeze from the branch's recorded tip would close routes 1a-1e, but it may need a check-ruling on the fixture.

Checks to add, each to be seen red against dce59515: the ledger moved out of the working copy; a hand-written integrate entry; `git --work-tree=<other>`; an uncommitted edit of an example's concept tag, then supersede or retire; an uncommitted edit dropping a check's import; `workPackage update --output` covering a used file; an in-place rewrite, deletion or second define of a frozen concept's journal entry; `git push . <sha>:refs/heads/<b>` and a push from a clone; a linked worktree under the husky wiring; `git replace` followed by an ordinary commit.

Over-refusal: a builder's `git merge main` or `git rebase main` onto the architect's committed example correction is refused. The gate charges whoever moves the branch for every frozen-path difference between the two tips, including changes the architect already recorded, so no non-architect can carry the correction to another branch.

`concepts define` never consults the freeze. The lead can record the first meaning of a concept a frozen cut's examples name but the journal lacks (seen admitted, journal and commit). Under an unreadable ledger `define` is also admitted, though 0129 says every journal change to a concept is then refused.
`unchecked` counts an example as bound when any frozen file mentions '<context>/<n>', read from the working copy, so a frozen non-check file, or an uncommitted mention, meets the dispatch gate.

[INFERENCE from render.ts, not run live] Only `bash` calls name the agent. The extension deletes the ambient CRATYLUS_AGENT, so an architect's git commit through omp's eval tool runs as an unknown agent and is refused. That fails safe, but it refuses the architect.
0130 says 'the freeze's wording says so', but the freeze concept's current version says nothing about set-by-hand names or switched-off hooks. Only the cli README does.
